description: Employee Referral This position may be eligible for an employee referral bonus. Please review the Employee Referral Bonus Instructions for information on steps or contact your HR representative. Company Information PACCAR is a Fortune 500 company established in 1905. PACCAR is a global technology leader in the design, manufacture and customer support of premium light-, medium- and heavy-duty trucks under the Kenworth, Peterbilt and DAF nameplates and provides customized financial services, information technology and truck parts related to its principal business. Whether you want to design the transportation technology of tomorrow, support the staff functions of a dynamic, international leader, or build our excellent products and services, you can develop the career you desire with PACCAR. Get started! Requisition Summary PACCAR is seeking a Senior Commodity Manager to join a strong and growing Purchasing team. In this role, one will negotiate and manage all aspects of PACCAR’s relationship with suppliers, including the commercial/contractual requirements with respect to total cost, technology, delivery, customer service, aftermarket support, logistics and quality. Commodity Managers are change agents, focused on delivering the highest value to internal and external customers at the lowest total cost. A successful candidate will demonstrate outstanding time management, organizational skills, and the ability to run multiple projects/tasks simultaneously. This position will be based out of the PACCAR Corporate Office located in Bellevue, WA . Job Functions / Responsibilities Develop, negotiate, and implement strategies resulting in effective cost management, improved supply chain performance and enhanced product quality. Investigate, evaluate, and implement new strategic procurement and logistics opportunities. Negotiate and ensure supplier compliance to long-term supply and warranty agreements. Issue formal Requests for Information, Proposals and Quotes (RFIs, RFPs, and RFQs) and analyze responses to select suppliers that meet or exceed PACCAR requirements Collaborate with PACCAR operations teams to successfully develop and execute global supply chain and commodity strategies. Organize and conduct supplier performance management (SPM) meetings, other cross-functional meetings, and formal presentations with suppliers, plant, and division personnel at all management levels. Travel to supplier locations to evaluate capabilities, assess production readiness, investigate new opportunities, improve manufacturing efficiencies and resolve chronic supply and quality issues. Travel to PACCAR’s operating locations in support of the above activities Qualifications & Skills 7+ years of work experience. Minimum of 5 years of purchasing, supply chain, or materials. Ability to effectively communicate verbally and in writing to various levels of management and suppliers. Experienced negotiator with demonstrated favorable results. Possess a strong understanding of fundamental contract terms and be able to draft supply contracts. Experience with sourcing to support new product development and develop sourcing strategies. Successfully manage supplier through all phases of a product development program. Perform advanced analysis on large data sets using Excel, draw salient conclusions from such analysis, and cogently present analysis to management. Ability to conceptualize and implement cost savings projects. Ability to direct oneself and act with minimal supervision. Be able to influence supplier behavior to meet PACCAR requirements. Possess an understanding of cost drivers and how changes in those drivers affect cost. Ability to conduct market research to identify and evaluate potential new suppliers. Ability to develop sourcing strategies. Education Bachelor’s degree in business administration, engineering, supply chain management, or related field. Masters Degree or MBA (preferred). CPSM Certification (preferred). Paccar Benefits As a U.S. PACCAR employee, you have a full range of benefit options including: Competitive salary and 401k with up to a 5% company match Fully funded pension plan that provides monthly benefits after retirement Comprehensive paid time off – Minimum of 10 paid vacation days, 12 paid holidays, and sick leave Tuition reimbursement for continued education Medical, dental, and vision plans for you and your family Flexible spending accounts (FSA) and health savings account (HSA) Paid short-and long-term disability program Life and accidental death and dismemberment insurance EAP services including wellness plans, estate planning, financial counseling and more Global Fortune 500 company with a wide array of growth and development opportunities Work alongside experienced goal-oriented colleagues recognized as experts in their field Additional Job Board Information PACCAR is an Equal Opportunity Employer/Protected Veteran/Disability. At PACCAR, we value talent and promote growth and development. We carefully consider numerous compensation factors, including your education, training, or experience. The salary range for Senior Commodity Manager is $104,100 - $162,900 annually. Additionally, this role is eligible for a full range of benefit options listed above.

description: About Veeco You probably don’t realize it, but what we do at Veeco touches the lives of every person, every day. It’s a bold statement, but it’s true. Along with the world’s leading technology companies, many of which are household names, we help solve their most difficult material science challenges, enabling technologies for a more connected, sustainable, and convenient world. Build category plans that align product roadmaps and production requirements with cost objectives and long-term supply resilience. Negotiate pricing, lead times, capacity commitments, payment terms, intellectual property protections, warranties, service levels, and other complex commercial terms. Develop alternate-source, inventory, capacity, and recovery strategies with cross-functional stakeholders. Deliver compelling, data-driven category strategies, risk assessments, tradeoffs, and recommendations to leadership, influencing timely decisions without direct authority. description: Job Description Oracle is seeking a Senior Strategic Sourcing Manager to lead end-to-end sourcing strategy for CPUs, silicon-based products, and emerging technologies supporting Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) and on-premises platforms. This highly visible role will manage strategic supplier relationships across critical infrastructure categories where cost, capacity, technology roadmaps, and continuity of supply are essential to Oracle's growth. You will lead commercial negotiations, develop pricing and sourcing strategies, support long-term capacity planning, and drive initiatives that strengthen supply-chain resiliency and supplier performance. Working closely with Engineering, Product, Supply Chain, and business leadership, you will translate technical and business requirements into executable supplier strategies. The successful candidate will be comfortable operating independently in a fast-paced, complex, and ambiguous environment and influencing decisions across Oracle and its strategic supplier ecosystem. Responsibilities RESPONSIBILITIES Develop and execute sourcing strategies for CPUs, silicon-based products, and related infrastructure components. Lead strategic supplier relationships and serve as a primary interface between Oracle and key suppliers. Lead complex commercial negotiations involving pricing, contracts, capacity, supply commitments, and business terms. Develop long-term sourcing and capacity strategies aligned with product, technology, and infrastructure roadmaps. Partner with Engineering and Product teams to understand technical requirements, supplier capabilities, technology roadmaps, and sourcing trade-offs. Drive competitive cost, supplier performance, supply assurance, and supply-chain efficiencies across assigned categories. Identify supply, capacity, commercial, and supplier risks and develop strategies to improve resiliency and continuity of supply. Evaluate supplier and market dynamics to support sourcing decisions, negotiations, and long-term planning. Lead cross-functional initiatives involving multiple Oracle lines of business and external suppliers. Create and implement sourcing and supply-chain process improvements that drive efficiency and establish scalable best practices. Navigate complex and ambiguous business situations using balanced judgment, analytical thinking, and structured problem solving. Build constructive stakeholder relationships and influence decisions across technical, business, and supplier organizations. Provide direction and mentorship to colleagues while promoting agility, adaptability, and continuous improvement. Qualifications 8+ years of relevant experience in strategic sourcing, procurement, supply chain, supplier management, commodity management, or a related field preferred. BA/BS degree preferred. Experience supporting CPU, silicon, semiconductor, or closely adjacent technology categories strongly preferred. Demonstrated experience leading commercial negotiations, pricing strategy, contracting, and strategic supplier relationships. Experience with capacity planning, constrained supply, supply assurance, risk mitigation, or supply-chain resiliency. Ability to understand technical and commercial considerations and translate them into actionable sourcing strategies. Strong cross-functional collaboration and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to influence across Engineering, Product, Supply Chain, business leadership, and suppliers. Strong analytical, problem-solving, negotiation, and communication skills. Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced environment where work is non-routine, complex, and sometimes ambiguous. description: Job Details Job Description: The Role and Impact As a Sr. Commodity Manager within the GMO Litho Materials Organization, you will drive Intel's supply chain excellence for Litho materials by optimizing cost, ensuring supply continuity, and enabling technology roadmap execution. You will shape sourcing strategies, build strategic supplier partnerships, and influence both commercial and technical decisions to strengthen Intel's competitive position. Within this group, the Global Sourcing Equipment and Materials Organization drives supplier strategies and supply chain solutions that align with Intel's technology roadmaps and ensure long-term sustainability. This team plays a critical role in Intel's mission to deliver high-quality products and services efficiently and effectively to customers worldwide. Qualifications This position is not eligible for Intel immigration sponsorship. Minimum Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, Engineering, or a related field, with 6+ years of relevant experience OR Master's degree in a related field with 4+ years of relevant experience. 4+ years of experience in the following: Contracting, negotiating, and supplier relationship management. Supply chain fundamentals, market dynamics, and risk mitigation strategies. Data analysis tools, such as Power BI and Microsoft Excel. Commodity management and program management. Preferred Qualifications Experience in semiconductor or manufacturing industries. Experience with material management Familiarity with Intel's purchasing policies and tools, such as Ariba. Proficiency in developing ROI models and cost analysis strategies. Leadership skills to drive results and manage ambiguity. Exceptional communication and collaboration skills to engage diverse stakeholders. We invite you to join Intel and contribute to shaping the future of technology. Be a part of a team that drives innovation, sustainability, and operational excellence in a dynamic global environment. Job Type Experienced Hire Shift Shift 1 (United States of America) Primary Location: US, Oregon, Hillsboro Additional Locations: US, Arizona, Phoenix Posting Statement All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, religious creed, sex, national origin, ancestry, age, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, military and veteran status, marital status, pregnancy, gender, gender expression, gender identity, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by local law, regulation, or ordinance. description: Job Description Oracle is seeking a Senior Strategic Sourcing Manager to lead end-to-end sourcing strategy for CPUs, silicon-based products, and emerging technologies supporting Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) and on-premises platforms. This highly visible role will manage strategic supplier relationships across critical infrastructure categories where cost, capacity, technology roadmaps, and continuity of supply are essential to Oracle's growth. You will lead commercial negotiations, develop pricing and sourcing strategies, support long-term capacity planning, and drive initiatives that strengthen supply-chain resiliency and supplier performance. Working closely with Engineering, Product, Supply Chain, and business leadership, you will translate technical and business requirements into executable supplier strategies. The successful candidate will be comfortable operating independently in a fast-paced, complex, and ambiguous environment and influencing decisions across Oracle and its strategic supplier ecosystem. Responsibilities RESPONSIBILITIES Develop and execute sourcing strategies for CPUs, silicon-based products, and related infrastructure components. Lead strategic supplier relationships and serve as a primary interface between Oracle and key suppliers. Lead complex commercial negotiations involving pricing, contracts, capacity, supply commitments, and business terms. Develop long-term sourcing and capacity strategies aligned with product, technology, and infrastructure roadmaps. Partner with Engineering and Product teams to understand technical requirements, supplier capabilities, technology roadmaps, and sourcing trade-offs. Drive competitive cost, supplier performance, supply assurance, and supply-chain efficiencies across assigned categories. Identify supply, capacity, commercial, and supplier risks and develop strategies to improve resiliency and continuity of supply. Evaluate supplier and market dynamics to support sourcing decisions, negotiations, and long-term planning. Lead cross-functional initiatives involving multiple Oracle lines of business and external suppliers. Create and implement sourcing and supply-chain process improvements that drive efficiency and establish scalable best practices. Navigate complex and ambiguous business situations using balanced judgment, analytical thinking, and structured problem solving. Build constructive stakeholder relationships and influence decisions across technical, business, and supplier organizations. Provide direction and mentorship to colleagues while promoting agility, adaptability, and continuous improvement. Qualifications 8+ years of relevant experience in strategic sourcing, procurement, supply chain, supplier management, commodity management, or a related field preferred. BA/BS degree preferred. Experience supporting CPU, silicon, semiconductor, or closely adjacent technology categories strongly preferred. Demonstrated experience leading commercial negotiations, pricing strategy, contracting, and strategic supplier relationships. Experience with capacity planning, constrained supply, supply assurance, risk mitigation, or supply-chain resiliency. Ability to understand technical and commercial considerations and translate them into actionable sourcing strategies. Strong cross-functional collaboration and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to influence across Engineering, Product, Supply Chain, business leadership, and suppliers. Strong analytical, problem-solving, negotiation, and communication skills. Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced environment where work is non-routine, complex, and sometimes ambiguous. Qualifications Disclaimer: Certain U.S. based or U.S. customer or client-facing roles may be required to comply with applicable requirements, such as immunization/occupational health mandates, and/or drug testing requirements. Range and benefit information provided in this posting are specific to the stated locations only US: Hiring Range in USD from: $102,300 - $209,500 per year. May be eligible for bonus and equity. Oracle maintains broad salary ranges for its roles in order to account for variations in knowledge, skills, experience, market conditions and locations, as well as reflect Oracle's differing products, industries and lines of business. Candidates are typically placed into the range based on the preceding factors as well as internal peer equity. Oracle US offers a comprehensive benefits package which includes the following: Medical, dental, and vision insurance, including expert medical opinion Short term disability and long term disability Life insurance and AD&D Supplemental life insurance (Employee/Spouse/Child) Health care and dependent care Flexible Spending Accounts Pre-tax commuter and parking benefits 401(k) Savings and Investment Plan with company match Paid time off: Flexible Vacation is provided to all eligible employees assigned to a salaried (non-overtime eligible) position. Accrued Vacation is provided to all other employees eligible for vacation benefits. For employees working at least 35 hours per week, the vacation accrual rate is 13 days annually for the first three years of employment and 18 days annually for subsequent years of employment. Vacation accrual is prorated for employees working between 20 and 34 hours per week. Employees working fewer than 20 hours per week are not eligible for vacation. 11 paid holidays Paid sick leave: 72 hours of paid sick leave upon date of hire. Refreshes each calendar year. Unused balance will carry over each year up to a maximum cap of 112 hours. Paid parental leave Adoption assistance Employee Stock Purchase Plan Financial planning and group legal Voluntary benefits including auto, homeowner and pet insurance The role will generally accept applications for at least three calendar days from the posting date or as long as the job remains posted. Career Level - IC4 About Us Only Oracle brings together the data, infrastructure, applications, and expertise to power everything from industry innovations to life-saving care. And with AI embedded across our products and services, we help customers turn that promise into a better future for all. Discover your potential at a company leading the way in AI and cloud solutions that impact billions of lives. True innovation starts when everyone is empowered to contribute. That’s why we’re committed to growing a workforce that promotes opportunities for all with competitive benefits that support our people with flexible medical, life insurance, and retirement options. We also encourage employees to give back to their communities through our volunteer programs. We’re committed to including people with disabilities at all stages of the employment process. If you require accessibility assistance or accommodation for a disability at any point, let us know by emailing accommodation-request_mb@oracle.com or by calling 1-888-404-2494 in the United States. Oracle is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Oracle will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law.

description: Company Description Arista Networks is an industry leader in data-driven, client-to-cloud networking for large data center, campus and routing environments. What sets us apart is our relentless pursuit of innovation. We leverage the latest advancements in cloud computing, artificial intelligence, and software-defined networking to provide our clients with a competitive edge in an increasingly interconnected world. Our solutions are designed to not only meet the current demands of the digital landscape but to also anticipate and adapt to future challenges. At Arista we value the diversity of thought and perspectives that each employee brings to the table. We believe that fostering an inclusive environment, where individuals from various backgrounds and experiences feel welcome, is essential for driving creativity and innovation. Our commitment to excellence has earned us several prestigious awards, such as Best Engineering Team, Best Company for Diversity, Compensation, and Work-Life Balance. At Arista, we take pride in our track record of success and strive to maintain the highest standards of quality and performance in everything we do. Job Description Who You’ll Work With Arista is seeking a new Senior Commodity Manager, Rack Integration to support a brand new product segment, dealing with leading edge products for our most prominent customers. This is a critical role, ensuring that Arista Rack Integration business meets customer driven requirements, and supports revenue, quality and time to market. You will work with an experienced internal cross-disciplinary team, including product management, demand planning, product development, supply chain, manufacturing, and logistics. Externally you will help foster a strong network of technology and supply chain partners. We are looking for a hands-on leader, interested in being part of a world-class organization while building a strong functional team. Strong communications, problem solving, and communication skills are essential. What You’ll Do Collaborate with internal stake-holders to create, implement, and maintain strategic sourcing strategy for Arista’s Rack Integration to support customer & company requirements. Ownership of RFP process, proposal evaluation & supplier assessment, and supplier selection. Manage the relationship with key Rack Integration partners as well as material suppliers. Coordinate with our product management team, engineering team, material team and integration partners to assure timely delivery of all prototypes and production units to our customers. In partnership with NPI engineers, lead efforts around capacity planning and capex roll out Negotiations and management of cost models for suppliers to include hard requirements (such as price, volume discounts, etc.) and soft requirements (such as expertise, technical backup, etc.) in the context of Total Acquisition Cost (TAC) and Total Opportunity Cost (TOC). Identification and delivery of opportunities for cost reduction. Lead negotiator for contract negotiations (SOWs, MPAs, LTAs, Development Agreements, etc.) Ensures appropriate performance measure (Technology, Quality, Cost and Delivery) of supply base and feedback of results through regular QBRs. Working with the site supply chain leads, this individual will manage relationships with suppliers on behalf of Arista. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Business, Supply Chain Management, Operations or Engineering required; Master’s degree preferred. Minimum 10 years’ experience in a networking environment with mechanical commodity and material management positions. Combined new product introduction, operations, and supplier management experience is highly desirable. Understanding of rack integration industry, component vendors ecosystem, and manufacturing processes Experience working and negotiating with external partners Experience working with sales and external customers Proven ability to work effectively with cross-functional teams Excellent verbal and written communication. Ability to listen and simplify complex topics for non-technical audiences, and prepare summaries for executives and stakeholders Utilize strong team building abilities to lead cross-functional process improvement teams and lead change within the organization. Ability to coordinate cross-site, multi-functional objectives Additional Information Compensation Information: The new hire base pay for this role has a salary range of $142,000 to $188,000. Arista offers different pay ranges based on work location, so that we can offer consistent and competitive pay appropriate to the market. The actual base pay offered will be based on a wide range of factors, including skills, qualifications, relevant experience, and work location. The pay range provided reflects base pay only and in addition certain roles may also be eligible for discretionary Arista bonuses and equity. Employees in Sales roles are eligible to participate in Arista’s Sales Incentive Plan, which pays commissions calculated as a percentage of eligible sales. US-based employees are also entitled to benefits including medical, dental, vision, wellbeing, tax savings and income protection. The recruiting team can share more details during the hiring process specific to the role and location Arista Networks is an equal opportunity employer. Arista makes all hiring and employment-related decisions in a non-discriminatory manner without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin or any other factor determined to be unlawful under applicable federal, state, or law law. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

description: The group you’ll be a part of The Global Operations Group brings information systems, facilities, supply chain, logistics, and high-volume manufacturing together to drive the engine of our global business operations. We help Lam deliver industry-leading solutions with speed and efficiency, while actively supporting the resilient and profitable growth of Lam's business. The impact you’ll make As Senior Sourcing Manager, Lead the techno-commercial strategy for the Cables commodity by integrating engineering insight, supplier capability assessment, cost modelling, and commercial negotiation to enable scalable, reliable, and cost-competitive sourcing solutions. The role is accountable for influencing design decisions early, aligning sourcing strategy with technology roadmaps, developing supplier ecosystems, mitigating lifecycle risks, and delivering measurable business value across cost, quality, lead time, and supply resilience. What You’ll Do Define and execute the techno-commercial sourcing strategy for the Cables commodity, aligned with product, engineering, cost, and supply chain roadmaps. Partner with Engineering during early design stages to influence specifications, material choices, manufacturability, availability, and cost competitiveness. Translate technical requirements into supplier selection, sourcing decisions, commercial models, and long-term commodity strategies. Lead should-cost analysis, value engineering, cost breakdown reviews, and total cost of ownership discussions to drive cost reduction and cost avoidance. Evaluate supplier technical capabilities, manufacturing processes, capacity readiness, quality systems, and scalability to support current and future business needs. Drive commercial negotiations covering pricing, capacity, tooling, lead time, contractual terms, risk-sharing models, and supplier performance commitments. Act as the sourcing gatekeeper for new cable part introductions, ensuring alignment with commodity strategy, approved supplier roadmaps, and lifecycle risk plans. Develop alternate suppliers and OEM pathways to reduce single-source dependency, improve supply resilience, and support regional diversification objectives. Lead lifecycle risk management including obsolescence, technology transitions, compliance risks, capacity constraints, and alternate qualification plans. Collaborate cross-functionally with Engineering, Quality, Operations, Finance, Legal, and Program teams to deliver balanced technical and commercial outcomes. Success Measures Early design influence resulting in improved manufacturability, availability, and cost competitiveness. Sustained cost savings and cost avoidance through should-costing, negotiation, and value engineering. Reduced lead time and improved supply continuity through supplier development and capacity alignment. Improved supplier technical capability, scalability, and alternate sourcing readiness. Effective lifecycle risk mitigation across obsolescence, single-source exposure, and technology transitions. Strong cross-functional alignment between Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality, Operations, and Finance. Who We’re Looking For Bachelor’s degree in Electrical, Electronics, Mechanical, Industrial Engineering, Supply Chain, or a related field; advanced degree preferred. 15+ years of experience in strategic sourcing, commodity management, supplier development, or techno-commercial supply chain roles. Strong exposure to cables, harnesses, interconnects, electromechanical components, or comparable engineered commodities. Demonstrated ability to interpret technical requirements and translate them into sourcing strategy, supplier capability plans, and commercial outcomes. Proven experience in should-costing, value engineering, supplier negotiations, contract governance, and lifecycle risk management. Strong stakeholder influence, executive communication, analytical thinking, and cross-functional leadership skills. General shift, flexible to take meetings in SEA, India time zone Willing to travel 20% of the time locally and globally Preferred Qualifications Experience in semiconductor equipment, high-tech manufacturing, or complex engineered product environments. Exposure to global supplier ecosystems across India, Southeast Asia, China, Europe, or North America. Professional certification such as CPSM, CSCP, PMP, Lean Six Sigma, or equivalent supply chain / program management credential is desirable Our commitment We believe it is important for every person to feel valued, included, and empowered to achieve their full potential. By bringing unique individuals and viewpoints together, we achieve extraordinary results. Lam Research ("Lam" or the "Company") is an equal opportunity employer. Lam is committed to and reaffirms support of equal opportunity in employment and non-discrimination in employment policies, practices and procedures on the basis of race, religious creed, color, national origin, ancestry, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, marital status, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth and related medical conditions), gender, gender identity, gender expression, age, sexual orientation, or military and veteran status or any other category protected by applicable federal, state, or local laws. It is the Company's intention to comply with all applicable laws and regulations. Company policy prohibits unlawful discrimination against applicants or employees. Lam offers a variety of work location models based on the needs of each role. Our hybrid roles combine the benefits of on-site collaboration with colleagues and the flexibility to work remotely and fall into two categories – On-site Flex and Virtual Flex. ‘On-site Flex’ you’ll work 3+ days per week on-site at a Lam or customer/supplier location, with the opportunity to work remotely for the balance of the week. ‘Virtual Flex’ you’ll work 1-2 days per week on-site at a Lam or customer/supplier location, and remotely the rest of the time. Salary CA San Francisco Bay Area Salary Range for this position: Min $137,000 - Max $287,000. The above salary range for this position is relevant to applicants that reside or work onsite in the California, San Francisco Bay Area only. Salary offers will depend on factors that include the location you work from, your level, education, training, specific skills, years of experience and comparison to other employees already in this role. Actual salary may vary from salary offered due to numerous factors including but not limited to unpaid time off, unpaid leave, company mandated shutdown, and other relevant factors. Our Perks And Benefits At Lam, our people make amazing things possible. That’s why we invest in you throughout the phases of your life with a comprehensive set of outstanding benefits.

description: If you’re looking for a special place to build or grow your career, you’ve found it. Whether you’re an experienced professional, a recent college graduate or somewhere in between, IDEX is a place where you can apply your existing skills and learn new ones in an environment where you can make an impact. With interesting opportunities in engineering, marketing, sales, supply chain, operations, HR, finance, and more across more than 40 diverse businesses (https://www.idexcorp.com/our-businesses/business-segments/) around the globe, chances are, we have something special for you. SCOPE OF ROLE The Senior Commodity Manager – Performance Pneumatics is responsible for developing and executing global commodity strategies that support the Pneumatics Platform’s annual operating plan objectives for cost, quality, delivery, inventory, and supply continuity. This role provides strategic leadership across the assigned commodity portfolio, including supplier selection, negotiation, performance management, risk mitigation, and supply base optimization. The Senior Commodity Manager partners closely with Engineering, Operations, Quality, Finance, and Leadership to deliver year-over-year material productivity, support new product introductions, reduce complexity, improve supplier performance, and strengthen overall supply chain resilience. Essential Duties Strategic Sourcing & Supplier Management Develop and execute global commodity strategies that achieve annual operating plan targets for cost, quality, delivery, inventory, and supply continuity. Identify, evaluate, qualify, and develop suppliers to improve cost competitiveness, innovation, quality, supply chain resilience, and long term business growth. Leverage platform spend to lead supplier negotiations, establish commercial agreements, and secure the best total cost of ownership across assigned global commodities. Apply an 80/20 mindset to simplify the supply base, reduce product and supplier complexity, and improve sourcing effectiveness across the platform. Lead supplier development and continuous improvement initiatives with internal stakeholders to deliver measurable operational and financial results. Manage supplier performance through scorecards, executive business reviews, and corrective action plans focused on quality, delivery, cost, responsiveness, and capacity. Escalate critical issues when needed to protect business continuity and platform performance. Cost Management & Risk Mitigation Analyze market conditions, cost drivers, and supplier economics to identify and deliver sustainable cost reduction and overall value opportunities. Proactively assess and mitigate supply chain risks, including capacity constraints, sole-source exposure, geopolitical factors, logistics challenges, and supplier financial health and regional sourcing risks. Lead value engineering, resourcing, and productivity initiatives across the pneumatics platform to improve margin, reduce complexity and support long-term growth. Cross-Functional Collaboration & Leadership Partner with engineering and product development teams to align sourcing strategies with product roadmaps, technology changes, and growth priorities. Support new product introductions by ensuring supplier readiness, qualification, capacity, and risk management plans are in place. Work closely with quality, operations, engineering and finance to resolve supplier issues, improve performance, and drive corrective actions that protect business continuity. Lead and develop sourcing specialists to ensure alignment with platform sourcing strategies, priorities, and performance expectations. Education And Experience Requirements Or Equivalencies Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Engineering, Business, or a related discipline. 7–10 years of experience in sourcing, commodity management, or supply chain leadership within a manufacturing environment. Proven experience leading complex supplier negotiations, developing commercial agreements, and applying should-cost or cost modeling tools. Experience in commodities such as iron and aluminum castings, metal fabrication, machining, or other industrial components used in pneumatic products is preferred. Experience managing a global supply base, including supplier performance, capacity, and risk mitigation across regions. Lean manufacturing, continuous improvement, or supplier development experience is a plus. Demonstrated project management skills with the ability to lead cross-functional initiatives and drive results. Strong analytical, financial, Excel, ERP systems, and communication skills are required. Physical/Mental/Environmental Requirements Ability to manage multiple priorities with agility in a fast-paced manufacturing environment, solving problems quickly, and making sound decisions that balance risk, and business performance Promotes a growth-focused culture by challenging the status quo, embracing continuous improvement, and using 80/20 thinking to unlock speed, focus, and performance. Demonstrated ability to work effectively in a team environment while thinking independently, showing initiative, anticipating issues, and driving practical solutions. Strong analytical, interpersonal, and communication skills are required, along with the ability to influence cross-functional teams and suppliers at multiple levels of the organization. Leads with trust, team, and excellence by demonstrating accountability, integrity, sound judgment, and respect in interactions with colleagues, customers, and suppliers. Deliver results, not just updates, and hold self and others accountable for execution, follow-through, and business outcomes. Ability to travel approximately 20–30% domestically and internationally between business units and supplier locations as required. description: Build the Future of Data Center Cooling XNRGY is one of North America's fastest-growing manufacturers of sustainable HVAC and liquid cooling solutions for hyperscale and mission-critical data centers. description: Want to help shape tomorrow? At Bendix, we set the standard with advanced dynamic solutions that drive improved commercial vehicle performance and safety. We’re part of the Knorr-Bremse Group, the global leader in braking technologies. As part of our team, you’ll collaborate with a world of talented and dedicated colleagues whose sense of purpose complements your own. You’ll find rewarding opportunities, diverse experiences, partnerships, and an unwavering commitment to ethics and integrity. Bendix Commercial Vehicle Systems LLC is an Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) employer. It is the policy of the Company to provide equal employment opportunities to all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, protected veteran or disabled status, or genetic information. Purchasing and supply chain professional responsible for assigned electronic commodities, including printed circuit boards, electronic assemblies, wiring harnesses, semiconductors, connectors, sensors, and related components. Manages sourcing activities, supplier relationships, commercial agreements, cost reduction initiatives, supplier performance, and commodity results in support of Quality, Cost, Delivery, and business objectives. The scope and complexity of assignments, level of independent decision-making, and leadership expectations increase from Buyer 1 through Buyer 3. Essential Functions: Develop, implement, and manage sourcing and commodity strategies for assigned electronic components based on the level and complexity of the role. Evaluate and select suppliers, including global sourcing opportunities, supplier capability and risk assessments, negotiation of supply agreements, and rationalization of the supply base. Develop and execute cost reduction and productivity initiatives aligned with sourcing strategies, including negotiations, value engineering, design changes, supplier development, and supplier transitions. Support and/or lead purchasing activities for new product introductions, engineering changes, and product transfers to ensure sourcing, cost, quality, capacity, and timing requirements are met. Drive continuous improvement throughout the electronics supply chain through long-term agreements, value engineering, supplier development, and cross-functional collaboration. Develop and implement actions to achieve supply chain management objectives, including quality, delivery, productivity, inventory, and cost targets. Support and/or lead supplier quality and delivery improvement initiatives, including escalation and recovery planning for underperforming or high-risk suppliers. Develop and manage supplier relationships while supporting Bendix and Knorr-Bremse supply chain strategies and leveraging global synergies. Partner with Engineering, Supplier Quality, Manufacturing, Materials, Finance, and other stakeholders to resolve commercial and supply issues and support business requirements. Provide support to manufacturing locations regarding sourcing initiatives, supplier performance issues, capacity constraints, and Electronics CoC programs. Monitor electronics market conditions, technology trends, component availability, obsolescence, and supply continuity risks; develop and execute mitigation plans as appropriate. Maintain accurate purchasing data, sourcing documentation, contracts, and supplier records in applicable systems and in accordance with established processes. Knowledge: Knowledge of electronics sourcing and procurement practices, including market dynamics, lead times, lifecycle and obsolescence considerations, and supply continuity risks. Knowledge of printed circuit boards, electronic assemblies, wiring harnesses, semiconductors, connectors, sensors, and related electronic components. Knowledge of strategic sourcing, commodity management, supplier relationship management, contract development, and negotiation. Understanding of production control, material planning, inventory management, and ERP/MRP systems. Understanding of supplier quality, manufacturing processes, cost drivers, and value engineering principles. Knowledge of the legal, regulatory, and commercial requirements associated with purchasing goods domestically and internationally. Buyer 1 applies working knowledge of purchasing concepts and established processes. Buyer 2 applies sound knowledge to independently manage assigned commodities and complex sourcing activities. Buyer 3 applies advanced knowledge to develop strategy, address significant business risks, and guide cross-functional or regional initiatives. Experience: Buyer 1: Minimum 2–3 years of tactical purchasing, procurement, supply chain, or related experience. Manufacturing experience and exposure to electronics sourcing are preferred. Buyer 2: Minimum 3–5 years of tactical and strategic purchasing or procurement experience, including experience with electronic components or a comparable technical commodity. Manufacturing experience is preferred. Buyer 3: Minimum 5–7 years of progressive strategic and tactical purchasing or procurement experience, including significant experience sourcing electronic components and managing complex supplier relationships. Manufacturing experience is preferred. Experience working within a global purchasing organization and using ERP/MRP systems; SAP experience is preferred. Experience using multiple approaches to achieve cost reduction and supplier improvement, including negotiation, value engineering, design changes, and joint supplier programs. Experience supporting new product introductions, supplier transitions, and cross-functional projects is preferred. For Buyer 2 and Buyer 3, experience independently leading negotiations, sourcing projects, supplier escalations, and risk mitigation activities is expected. Buyer 3 experience should include leading complex initiatives and providing guidance to others. Skills: Ability to work effectively in a global matrix organization and collaborate across functions, regions, and cultures. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to evaluate cost, quality, delivery, capacity, and supply risk information and drive practical solutions. Ability to manage multiple priorities, quickly adjust to changing business needs, and maintain a high level of accuracy and attention to detail. Results-oriented with the ability to drive supplier improvement, cost reduction, productivity, and supply continuity actions. Self-starter with initiative, sound judgment, and the ability to work independently within the authority and expectations of the assigned level. Project management skills, including setting priorities, identifying risks and opportunities, coordinating resources, and managing milestones and costs in a cross-functional environment. Strong organization, planning, written communication, and verbal communication skills. Interpersonal and intercultural effectiveness with the ability to build productive supplier and internal stakeholder relationships. Negotiation and commercial skills appropriate to the assigned level: developing at Buyer 1, demonstrated at Buyer 2, and advanced at Buyer 3. Ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders. Buyer 2 may lead defined sourcing or supplier improvement projects. Buyer 3 is expected to lead complex initiatives, mentor less-experienced team members, and influence decisions across functions and regions. Proficiency with Microsoft Office and purchasing or ERP systems; ability to analyze data and clearly communicate recommendations. Education: Bachelor’s degree required in Business, Supply Chain Management, Engineering, or a related field. An equivalent combination of relevant education and directly related experience may be considered where permitted by company policy. Buyer 1: Co-op, internship, or other relevant purchasing, supply chain, manufacturing, or technical experience is a plus. Buyer 2: CPM, CPSM, CPIM, or Green Belt

description: About ITT ITT Inc. (NYSE: ITT) is a diversified global leading manufacturer of highly engineered critical components and customized technology solutions serving the flow, aerospace and defense, transportation, industrial, and energy markets. Through operational execution, innovation, and disciplined capital deployment, including strategic acquisitions such as SPX FLOW, ITT partners with its customers to deliver enduring solutions to the key industries that underpin our modern way of life. Headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut, ITT has a market cap of roughly $20 billion and employs more than 15,000 people across 40 countries and serves customers in approximately 125 countries. Following the acquisition of SPX FLOW, the company is expected to generate $5.4 billion in annual revenue. Our businesses are organized in three distinct segments, each based around our core engineering DNA: Flow Technologies: A global leader in, providing a broad portfolio of pumps, valves, mixing and agitation equipment, heat transfer, homogenizers, separation, water and wastewater treatment, and engineered process solutions.Our leading brands include the iconic Goulds Pumps (with more than 175 years of history), Anhydro, APV, Bornemann, Bran+Luebbe, C’treat, Engineered Valves, Gerstenberg Schröder, Habonim, Johnson Pump, Lightnin, Philadelphia, Plenty, PRO Cast, Rheinhütte, Seital Separation, Stelzer, Svanehøj, Tigerholm, Uutechnic, VIDAR, Waukesha Cherry-Burrell. Motion Technologies: A global leader in brake pads (ICE and electrified brake pads) and shock absorbers (energy absorption solutions) for transportation applications. Our leading brands include Friction Technologies, KONI and Axtone. Connect and Control Technologies: A leader in critical applications for the aerospace, defense and industrial markets, including harsh environment connectors and control components. Our leading brands include ITT Cannon, Enidine, Aerospace Controls and kSARIA. Position Summary Reporting directly to the Director, S trategic Sourcing for ITT (Connect & Control Technologies), the Global Sourcing Manager is a critical member of the Global Supply Management group responsible for enhancing overall supply chain performance through the effective management of ~$ 3 00M in global spend. This role is responsible for implementing ITT’s business strategy to your assigned categories and maintaining the best sources of supply. The Global Sourcing Manager is responsible for building strong supplier relationships and being proactive in mitigating supply chain challenges due to emerging economic trends around pricing, logistics , and geo-political risks. Working collaboratively with cross functional teams, this role will identify and champion complexity - reduction initiatives that will enhance profitability and service to customers. This is an on-site position that can be located in Orchard Park, Valencia, Irvine, or El Cajon, CA with up to 50% travel. Essential Responsibilities For the assigned categories, develop and implement sourcing / supply chain strategies to harness economies of scale, drive economic value, manage supply chain risk, and enable business growth at a global level in a multi-market-culture environment. Lead complex and critical negotiations utilizing extensive professional knowledge of principles and techniques of negotiation in the purchasing cycle. Provide global leadership for the major OEM suppliers. Research and evaluate suppliers based on price, quality, selection, service, support, availability, reliability, production and distribution capabilities, and the supplier's reputation and history. Leverage supplier management, category / commodity management and total cost principles to oversee the supplier selection process within the respective businesses / sites and encourage productive relationships with appropriate suppliers that drive meaningful value. Search, identify , qualify, develop, and manage suppliers to secure the best possible terms (cost, payment, inventory, etc . ) while ensuring operational performance (quality, OTD, lead time, cost, etc . ). Partner with engineering, manufacturing, quality and other category managers to drive value analysis and engineering (VAVE) savings. Partner with NPD teams to obtain early supplier engagement to set expectations, optimize quality, supply reliability, while reducing risk and cost for new product launches. Identify and introduce new materials, technologies, and supply chain capabilities to meet current and future needs of ITT products. Other responsibilities as assigned . Position Requirements Bachelor’s degree from an accredited 4-year college or university in Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, or equivalent is required . Minimum of 10 years of broad and global sourcing leadership experience, preferably in a highly regulated manufacturing organization, across a large multi-location, global business. Global Sourcing contract negotiation skills. Experience in a mixed mode manufacturing environment, Engineer to Order, Low Volume / High Mix, and Configure to Order environment. Strong interpersonal skills and ability to effectively interact with all levels of external and internal customers and stakeholders. Demonstrated experience influencing executives. Working knowledge of Lean practices such as Daily Management, Standard Work, Kaizen, Heijunka , Poka- yoke, and Gemba. Experience with a variety of commodities , including, but not limited to: precision metal machining, composites and plastics, injection molding, electronics and cables . Drive performance with a sense of urgency and a commitment to work together as a team to achieve results. D emonstrated success in a large-scale, global organization with the ability to work at both the strategic and detailed level. English fluency is required , while ability to communicate in one or more of the following languages is highly beneficial: German, Italian, French, Chinese (Mandarin / Cantonese) Travel up to 50% This position requires use of information which is subject to the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR). All applicants must be U.S. persons within the meaning of ITAR . ITAR defines a U.S. person as a U.S. Citizen, U.S. Permanent Resident ( i.e. 'Green Card Holder'), Political Asylee, or Refugee. Safety is a core value at ITT. Our employees understand and follow all ITT safety policies and procedures, participate in workplace inspections, safety training, and in the development of job safety analyses. Equal Pay Act Statement We aim to pay our ‘ITT’ers’ fairly and competitively in the locations that they live and work. Pay-for-performance is a principle that we believe in, and employees are rewarded based not only on ‘what’ they accomplish, but also on ‘how’ they reflect ITT’s values. ITT offers a competitive salary and robust total rewards package, such as health insurance, 401(k), short and long-term disability, paid time off, growth and developmental opportunities, and other incentive compensation programs. Specific benefits are dependent upon whether or not the position is part of a collective-bargaining agreement. The salary offered to a candidate is based several factors such as candidate experience and qualifications, location, as well as market and business considerations. Equal Pay Act Range Annual Salary Range is from $119,400.00 to $178,200.00, plus benefits & incentive plan.

description: MRO Commodity Manager Location: Highland Heights, KY Employment Type: Full Time | On-site Why Build Your Career with Prysmian? Your work at Prysmian helps power and connect the world. When you join Prysmian, you become part of a global team whose work touches millions of lives every day. You’ll help support the energy and digital infrastructure that keeps communities, businesses, and industries moving forward. For more than 140 years, Prysmian has helped shape the infrastructure that powers progress. From helping illuminate the Statue of Liberty in 1886 and delivering power from Hoover Dam to Los Angeles in 1935, to supporting New York City's rebuilding efforts after September 11, our cables and connectivity solutions have played a role in some of history's most significant milestones. Today, our impact continues. Prysmian products help power world class venues like Paycor Stadium, SoFi Stadium, and Lambeau Field. We're contributing to the infrastructure supporting the 2026 FIFA World Cup and the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles, helping ensure communities, businesses, and industries stay connected to what matters most. As an MRO Commodity Manager, you will manage sourcing activities, MRO service providers, and build strategic relationships throughout the company. What You’ll Bring Experience and Qualifications You have a bachelor’s degree in supply chain, Engineering, Business, Finance, Operations Management or a related field. You bring 5+ years of experience in strategic sourcing, procurement, project management, engineering procurement, or CAPEX procurement. You are proficient with ERP systems (SAP). You can travel approximately 50% of the time. What You’ll Do In this role you'll develop MRO category strategies, lead strategic supplier relationships, and negotiate pricing agreement and rebates. Develop and execute MRO sourcing strategies: You will reduce costs, drive standardization, strengthen supplier partnerships, and support regional and global procurement initiatives. Lead supplier management efforts: You’ll conduct performance reviews, track KPIs, drive continuous improvement, and resolve supply, quality, and commercial issues. Negotiate contracts and commercial agreements: You will negotiate pricing, service levels, inventory programs, payment terms, warranties, and other key business terms while ensuring policy compliance. Optimize MRO inventory and operational performance: You’ll partner with plant teams to improve spare parts strategies, reduce obsolete inventory, and enhance working capital. Serve as the primary procurement partner for MRO activities: You will manage over $150M in annual spend, support critical purchase orders, deliver savings targets, and collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders across manufacturing operations. You’ll have the opportunity to make an impact, build strong partnerships, and grow your career in a business that values ownership, collaboration, and continuous improvement. Total Rewards Designed for You We believe great people deserve great rewards. That’s why Prysmian offers a total rewards package designed to support your financial, physical, and personal well-being now and as your career grows. Competitive salary that recognizes your skills, experience, and contributions Performance-based incentives that reward your results and impact (where applicable) Comprehensive health coverage with medical, dental, and vision plan options to fit your needs 401(k) retirement savings plan with a competitive company match to help you invest in your future Paid maternity and bonding leave, plus adoption assistance to support you and your growing family Generous paid time off and company holidays so you can rest, recharge, and spend time on what matters most Life and disability insurance for added peace of mind Wellness programs and supplemental insurance options to support your overall health and well-being At Prysmian, you’ll be supported at work, at home, and throughout every stage of your career. Job Offer Fraud Alert We take the security of our candidates seriously. Please be aware of job offer scams involving individuals falsely claiming to represent our company. description: As a Market Sourcing Manager , you will be responsible for overall management of vendor negotiations and price setting of non-consumable products related to Grocery, Food Service, Janitorial and Processor business segments. Brand strategy, private label, and sustainable packaging product lines are important strategies managed by this position and integral to success in the role. In this role you will be an inventory strategy expert. Our National Category Manager team identifies our national core product list, which is the backbone of our inventory. As a Market Sourcing Manager, you will fill out the rest of our inventory with items required and acquired at the regional level. Can we get a core item, more efficiently from a local vendor? We need a specific item for a regional customer; who are we going to buy that from and at what terms? What are inventory and reorder thresholds for those items? How can we further lower margin on inventory by adding specific local inventory items as a preferred items for multiple local customers? These are the types of questions you'll make decisions on daily. This role is onsite in our Kansas City, MO office, M-F - day shift. There is some flexibility to work from home 1-2 days per month if needed. Responsibilities: Negotiate price and terms with manufacturers and suppliers. Product selection and sourcing. Develop market expertise that allows the organization to effectively compete in target market segments; this includes market trends and competitive analysis, as inputs to the development of our assortment strategy. Monitor market intelligence, local needs and trends, competitive products, and the changing production schedules of approved manufacturers to improve competitive pricing & positioning. Develop product pricing policies and negotiate best cost vendor programs to improve product positioning while improve margin. Rationalize and consolidate product lines to improve inventory turns and create volume cost improvement opportunities. Manage on-going supplier relationships and execute supplier performance management initiatives in accordance with standards and guidelines and in collaboration with business partners. Manage multiple projects and initiatives with the ability to meet defined timelines and provide proactive status communication to business partners. Work with sales staff with special product requirements and costing. Work to improve go-to-market strategy and speed. Problem solving and recommending new and different packaging products as they become available. Requirements: High school diploma or equivalent required Bachelor’s degree, strongly preferred Master’s degree preferred. 5+ years’ experience in price negotiations is required and influencing stakeholders at all levels. Knowledge of the distribution environment, inventory management systems, and supplier selection and qualification processes (ideally in food service, janitorial or packaging) Product knowledge across multiple industries a definite plus. Strong business and financial acumen Strong user level Microsoft Office skills (Outlook, Excel, TEAMs) Ability to create excellent relationships and quickly gain credibility with internal and external stakeholders. Possess strong planning, organizational and time management skills, as well as strong analytical problem-solving skills. Multi-task with the ability to change direction quickly and often. What's in it for you? The perks of being a Bunzl team member don’t stop at being part of a great team or being valued as our #1 asset. We offer a full range of benefits to help our employees take care of themselves and their families today, tomorrow and for the future. Medical, Dental & Vision Benefits effective the 1st day of the month after 30 days Paid Time Off - Vacation, Sick, Holidays and Personal Time 401K with generous company match Additional benefit information can be found on the Bunzl Careers home page under Benefits and Perks. Bunzl accepts ongoing applications for this role until it is filled. What are you waiting for? A new career awaits you with endless opportunities. Bunzl is a global leader in the Cleaning & Hygiene, Food Processing, Grocery, Health Care, Non-Food Retail, and Safety industries. We have grown both organically and through acquisitions to sales in excess of $10 billion. Bunzl North America is headquartered in St. Louis, Missouri. Bunzl North America owns and operates more than 100 warehouses and serves all 50 states, Puerto Rico, Canada and parts of the Caribbean and Mexico. With more than 5,000 employees and 400,000 plus supplies, Bunzl is regarded as a leading supplier in North America. Bunzl Distribution has a tradition of commitment to equal employment opportunity. It is the established policy to attract and retain the best qualified people without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex/gender (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, age, disability or veteran status as provided by law. description: Who we are About Stripe Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career. About The Team Procurement is part of Stripe Finance and owns the full supplier lifecycle and buying journey. The team sources and evaluates new vendors, renews and negotiates contracts with existing suppliers, and leads third‑party risk management and compliance activities to ensure suppliers meet Stripe’s standards. Procurement also drafts, reviews, and approves supplier contract structures and terms, aligned with Stripe’s risk appetite and legal requirements. What you’ll do We are looking for an experienced Sourcing professional to focus on establishing trusted business partner relationships in the technology space at Stripe with a “users first” approach to ensure early and active participation across the full lifecycle of strategic sourcing and procurement, including: category planning, sourcing strategies, RFx execution, supplier evaluation and selection, contract negotiations and management, and continuous improvements. You will play a critical role in ensuring Stripe's procurement aligns with our operational principles by contributing to our sustainable growth while fostering strong, ethical supplier relationships. Experience with complex software negotiations is required. Responsibilities Develop and execute strategic sourcing plans for designated categories, identifying opportunities for cost reduction, quality improvement, and process efficiencies Lead supplier selection, assessment, and contract negotiation processes, ensuring compliance with Stripe's policies and risk management protocols Conduct market research and analysis to inform category strategies and stay ahead of industry trends Be an active champion across the company supporting our third party risk programs and fiscal initiatives when engaging in Procurement activities Deliver on strategic sourcing management goals including cost savings and spend under management, and implement any necessary process enhancements to ensure that those goals are achieved Evaluate existing supplier base and identify rationalization and/or RFx opportunities in partnership with business teams and Finance, allowing Stripe to maximize negotiating leverage Work closely with internal teams to drive enterprise-level procurement solutions and increase supplier management effectiveness Participate in establishing short-term and long range planning and budget development of the company to support strategic business goals Help to develop and execute a roadmap to build and scale an impactful Strategic Sourcing & Category Management function that Stripes recognize and value Who you are We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement. Minimum Requirements A minimum of 8 years of experience in indirect sourcing, procurement, category management, or a related field Demonstrated ability to develop and implement strategic sourcing and category management strategies Proven negotiation skills and a track record of achieving significant cost savings and supplier value without compromising on quality or service Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage and interpret complex data Experience in supplier contracting with a solid understanding of standard commercial terms and conditions to mitigate risks and create clear service level agreements Leadership and stakeholder management skills with the ability to elevate ambitions and influence cross-functional and internal team members Preferred Qualifications Solution-oriented mindset with enthusiasm for establishing best practice Self-disciplined, diligent, proactive and detail oriented Comfort with a rapid pace of change, complexity, and working across matrixed functions, preferably within a fast-paced technology or financial services environment Strategic mindset with the ability to make sound business decisions based on data and analytics Understanding or experience with e-procurement tools and systems (e.g., Zip, Workday Strategic Sourcing, Oracle, etc.) Familiarity with the fintech industry and its supply chain and procurement challenges In-office expectations Office-assigned Stripes in most of our locations are currently expected to spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This expectation may vary depending on role, team and location. For example, Stripes in Stripe Delivery Center roles in Mexico City, Mexico, Bengaluru, India, and Dublin, Ireland work 100% from the office. Also, some teams have greater in-office attendance requirements, to appropriately support our users and workflows, which the hiring manager will discuss. This approach helps strike a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility when possible. Pay and benefits The annual US base salary range for this role is $136,000 - $204,000. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process. Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends. We look forward to hearing from you. At Stripe, we're looking for people with passion, grit, and integrity. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. Your skills and passion will stand out—and set you apart—especially if your career has taken some extraordinary twists and turns. At Stripe, we welcome diverse perspectives and people who think rigorously and aren't afraid to challenge assumptions. Join us. Apply now Please find our California applicant personal information notice here.

Develop and implement strategies to manage long lead-time and unique components effectively. Prepare and analyze inventory and aging reports to optimize supply chain efficiency. Support demand planning and forecast reviews with suppliers to ensure adequate supply capacity. Monitor supplier lead times, production capacity, and delivery commitments to minimize supply disruptions Process Improvement & Strategic Planning Identify opportunities to improve procurement accuracy and streamline supply chain processes. Implement best practices to optimize resource utilization and cost savings. Support cross-functional teams in forecasting, demand planning, and risk mitigation strategies. Lead supplier cost reduction initiatives through commercial negotiations, alternative sourcing, and value engineering. Develop sourcing risk mitigation plans for sole-source and long lead-time components. Track and report sourcing KPIs, including cost savings, supplier performance, on-time delivery, and sourcing cycle time. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Materials Management, Manufacturing, or a related discipline preferred. 8+ years of experience in materials management, procurement, or supply chain operations. description: Senior Buyer, U.S. Operations Location: Boulder CO United States (On-Site) Department: Supply Chain / Procurement We’re Expanding Our Supply Chain Team! Are you ready to lead high-impact procurement initiatives with a dynamic, high-growth company? We are looking for a strategic, results-driven Senior Buyer to join our team. This role is ideal for an experienced procurement professional looking to own end-to-end strategic sourcing, drive category management, and lead complex commercial negotiations within the renewable energy and energy storage industry. You will spearhead high-value sourcing strategies, manage critical supplier partnerships, and play a pivotal role in scaling our Source-to-Pay (S2P) operations. You’ll work closely with executive leadership and cross-functional teams to mitigate supply chain risks, optimize cost structures, and support large-scale project deployment. This role includes a travel requirement of approximately 15-25% for key supplier negotiations, site visits, and operational coordination. If you have a passion for strategic sourcing, complex contracting, and driving continuous improvement in a fast-paced environment, we’d love to hear from you. Key Responsibilities Lead the end-to-end Source-to-Pay (S2P) lifecycle for critical project categories; develop and execute RFPs/RFQs, drive complex commercial bid evaluations, and architect high-value supplier contracts. Serve as the strategic escalation point for key suppliers; conduct regular business reviews, monitor long-term performance KPIs, mitigate commercial risks, and drive continuous supplier improvement. Partner seamlessly with Engineering, Project Management, Quality, Legal, and Finance teams to align procurement strategies with major project milestones, capital budgets, and execution timelines in an EPC driven environment. Negotiate favorable commercial terms, pricing agreements, warranties, and service level agreements (SLAs) while partnering with legal counsel to minimize risk and ensure corporate compliance. Conduct total cost of ownership (TCO) analyses, monitor global market trends for key commodities, generate executive-level reports, and identify cost-optimization opportunities. Drive internal procurement process improvements, maintain rigorous audit readiness within ERP systems. Key Competencies Advanced price negotiation and cost reduction Strategic sourcing and competitive bidding Contract drafting and commercial risk management Cross-functional leadership and stakeholder management Financial acumen and TCO (Total Cost of Ownership) analysis Advanced data analysis and market intelligence Project management and timeline execution Problem-solving and critical thinking Change management and continuous improvement Executive communication and presentation skills Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in supply chain management, Business Administration, Engineering, Finance, or a related field. 6–8+ years of progressive experience in strategic sourcing, purchasing, contract management, or supply chain operations, ideally within industrial, manufacturing, construction, or energy sectors. description: JOB SUMMARY The Senior Planner/Buyer, Contract Manufacturing is appointed to their position by the Supervisor, Contract Manufacturing Supply Chain. This role ensures optimal inventory levels, efficient production planning, and timely product availability while maintaining strong supplier partnerships and driving continuous improvement across cost, quality, and service. The position collaborates cross-functionally with Marketing, Sales, Quality, R&D, Regulatory, and Distribution teams to support new product introductions, maintain production schedules, and uphold company standards for performance and compliance.   ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS Analyze inventory levels for contract manufactured finished goods, work-in-process (WIP), and related primary and secondary packaging materials. Create and manage purchase orders in alignment with Demand and MRP Plans to ensure product availability while minimizing excess and obsolescence risk. Maintain and update the Master Production Schedule for designated contract manufactured items Build and strengthen partnerships with designated contract manufacturers, ensuring accountability for performance, quality, and service excellence. Monitor supplier performance, lead times, backorders, investigations, and delivery commitments, proactively addressing risks to prevent or minimize out-of-stock situations. Review pricing updates and purchase price variances to identify opportunities for cost reduction and process improvement. Plan and coordinate component shipments to contract manufacturers, ensuring accurate documentation and alignment with distribution center operations. Create and manage Bills of Material (BOMs) for all assigned contract manufacturers, ensuring proper routing and approval within MasterControl. Maintain organized and up-to-date records of pricing, supplier data, and contracts to enable timely and accurate access to information. Review and approve invoices in accordance with company policies and financial controls. Prepare and distribute monthly forecast updates to key stakeholders as required.  Collaborate with Quality, R&D, and Regulatory teams to plan and execute line trials for new materials or validate new projects as assigned. Partner with Marketing and cross-functional teams to support new product innovations, ensuring timely commercialization and seamless supply chain readiness for product launches.   ADDITIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES Performs and assumes other duties and responsibilities, as may be required by the Supervisor, Contract Manufacturing Supply Chain. Keep the Supervisor, Contract Manufacturing Supply Chain duly informed of all activities, including significant problems and achievements. Supports cGMP, the Winner’s Circle, and the Blistex Quality System.   REQUIRED EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS Experience within consumer packaged goods (CPG), food, pharmaceutical, or other regulated manufacturing industries. Minimum of 5+ years of progressive experience in supply chain planning, procurement, or production management, with a strong focus on contract manufacturing operations. Strong understanding of MRP, Demand Planning, and inventory management principles. Proven ability to manage and negotiate with contract manufacturers and suppliers to achieve business objectives.
